title: Listing Exception Decision Log and Copy Atomization
body:
Purpose:
This is a working decision log and a lightweight ‘copy atom’ catalogue for listing exceptions. Goal: speed up reviewer decisions for non-standard partner listings and produce a small, reusable set of copy fragments that engineers and creative can pick from when we need fast edits for edge-case listings.

Scope and usage notes:
- Use for partner listings that deviate from default SKU, billing, or compliance patterns (e.g., reseller matrix, non-metered trials, or pre-approved regional variants).
- Each entry in the decision log should include date, owner, brief rationale, impacted assets, and follow-ups.
- Copy atoms below are intentionally short; they must be used verbatim in tile text and trimmed into hero, subhead, and badges.

Decision log (chronological, tentative):
1) 2025-11-10 — Marco Nguyen — Approved temporary non-metered 90-day trial for EDU pilot (partner: ScholarCloud). Rationale: partner has institutional billing; need short runway to measure adoption. Impact: trial badge, billing SKU mapping, trial conversion metrics. Follow-up: meter conversion gating (JIRA-3210).
2) 2025-12-08 — Leah Brooks — Denied per-region image substitution for EU partner tile (security/audit mismatch). Rationale: variant changes obscured data residency claims. Impact: partner asked for localized image; suggested replace with neutral screenshot. Owner to re-submit 2026-01-05.
3) 2026-01-18 — Aisha Patel — Exception approved for alternate CTA flow (‘Request a Dedicated Demo’) for enterprise partners on offer page; must link to SSO form and include SLA blurb. Follow-up: add SLA snippet to copy atom pool and update routing docs (JIRA-3399).

Acceptance criteria checklist for exception approvals:
- Legal/compliance sign-off (email thread required)
- Billing SKU mapping confirmed with Finance (billing-code present)
- Technical gate: SSO/KMS/checkbox verified for private deployments if relevant
- UX sanity check: no misleading claims about latency/SLA beyond what we support
- Localization: partner-provided translations validated (if included)

Copy atom catalogue (use-case tagged in brackets) — short, pickable lines:
- Hero-Short: "Low-latency inference, predictable costs" [hosted-summary]
- Hero-Alt: "Run large language models with enterprise SLAs" [enterprise-hero]
- Subhead-1: "Deploy across hosted, dedicated, and private environments" [product-surface]
- Feature-Bullet-1: "Per-route latency SLAs and token-level cost breakdowns" [obs]
- Feature-Bullet-2: "Dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling and burst capacity" [dedicated]
- CTA-Primary: "Start free — 14-day trial" [trial-cta]
- CTA-Ent: "Request a dedicated demo" [enterprise-cta]
- Badge-Trial: "14-day trial — no credit card needed" [trial-badge]
- Badge-EDU: "Academic pilot — contact sales" [edu-badge]
- Security-Blurb: "Data isolated with customer-controlled keys (KMS/HSM)" [security]
- Small Disclaimer: "Model variants may differ in latency and token cost" [disclaimer]

Copy variants and micro-templates (examples):
- Tile (short): "Redwood Inference — predictable LLM inference. Start free."
- Tile (enterprise): "Redwood Inference — SLA-backed LLM serving for teams. Request demo."
- Long description (200–300 chars): "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime to serve large language models across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Reduce token costs with intelligent caching and batching while keeping SLAs and data controls for regulated workloads."

Technical & ops preflight for exceptions:
- Confirm metering: is partner using our metered token plan or a commit? (answer: note in log)
- Billing SKU: map to internal SKU and confirm marketplace SKU exists (Finance sign-off required)
- OAuth/SSO: for enterprise CTAs, ensure SSO redirect URI is provisioned and tested
- Artifacts: ensure creative assets meet marketplace dimension guidelines; if not, mark exception and request neutral screenshot
- Privacy: verify if data residency claim is in copy — if yes, attach compliance review doc

Localization and accessibility notes:
- When accepting translated copy atoms, require a side-by-side English source and a native-speaker reviewer (team recommendation: Solutions Eng or partner translator)
- Badge text must be under 28 characters to avoid truncation in APAC tiles

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide permanent threshold for non-metered trials: should we allow only EDU/NGO or also early-stage ISVs? (owner: Go-to-market, due 2026-03-01)
- Add a short FAQ snippet for listing exceptions that can be surfaced in partner onboarding materials
- Create a tiny UI in the partner portal that flags active exceptions for ops teams (request to product backlog: JIRA-3502)

Quick links & references:
- Confluence: marketplace onboarding overview — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GTM/marketplace-onboarding
- Jira: JIRA-3210 (trial conversion gate), JIRA-3399 (enterprise CTA routing), JIRA-3502 (exception flagging UI)
- Slack: #marketplace-partners thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345

Next steps (short):
- Finalize EDU trial gating language and add to badge pool (owner: Marco) by 2026-02-28
- Publish canonical copy atoms to design/system repo and link in partner portal (owner: Leah) by 2026-03-10
- Create acceptance checklist template in Confluence and link from partner intake form (owner: Aisha) by 2026-03-05

Notes to self: keep entries terse, prefer re-usable atoms over bespoke paragraphs. This is a working file — share in the next GTM weekly sync for alignment and push any approved exceptions into the formal marketplace runbook.
